parameters: \c[6](A book detailing the conception of the Ultimate System...)
\c[6](It seems to explain that in a time of dire need the government conceived the
concept of Ultimates to provide the public with figures of guidance and prosperity.
They were responsible for paving the way for a better future.)
\c[6](They decided to scout a majority of Ulitmates from a young age as younger minds
are more easily influenced.)
\c[6](The book seems to paint Ultimates in a positive light.)
\c[6](A story about a maid who was bossed around all day.)
\c[6](The maid grew sick of it and took on a deal with the devil.)
\c[6](Signing away her soul and morality for an easy and secure life.)
\c[6](In return she would do the devil's bidding.)
\c[6](However, she soon grew sick of it and started running away from him.)
\c[6](The Devil failed to see why she deserved a normal life, especially after all
the poisonings the selfish maid did for the Devil in exchange for her riches.)
\c[6](And so he would chase her, something the Maid was aware of.)
\c[6](Eager to save herself, the selfish maid would frequently leave whoever protected her.
And leave their souls and bodies to placate/entertain the devil in her stead.)
\c[6](Despite her words, she never truly obtained a moral godly life. This was the way she'd
always known, it was the way things would continue.)
\c[6](So the Maid appeared to actually be a scorpion. And the devil feasted on her
frogs.)
\c[6](A story about a little Princess...)
\c[6](This Little Princess was surrounded by guests constantly.)
\c[6](Some guests frustrated or annoyed the Princess-)
\c[6](One day, in her frustration, she called one of the guests a witch.)
\c[6](And they were promptly burnt at the stake.)
\c[6](The Little Princess took joy in this.)
\c[6](And from that day, the Princess seemed to discover Witches frequently in her court.)
\c[6](A story about a little leapfrog who could bounce and play with their tadpole friends
all day.)
\c[6](This little leapfrog supported all the creatures of the pond.)
\c[6](But they held a dark and terrible secret...)
\c[6](The little leapfrog was actually a moth in disguise.)
\c[6](They used their illusions to create a light they'd coveted their whole life.)
\c[6](And made the tadpoles swim in spirals to create their own illusions to brighten this
light.)
\c[6](Folks came from far and wide to see this light the leapfrog and the tadpoles
had made... Unaware it was all an illusion, a lie.)
\c[6](They praised the little leapfrog and showered them in gifts to feed the light.)
\c[6](The leapfrog, breaking illusion, would devour these gifts.)
\c[6](And would slowly one by one, grant each tadpole moth wings.)
\c[6](It's a fairytale about a young witch!)
\c[6](She set out to find immortality to save a dear friend.)
\c[6](However, the path to immortality came at a cost...)
\c[6](The witch tested various magical cures on her animal friends!)
\c[6](Most didn't end very well... Many of the animals becoming very different!)
\c[6](But the witch didn't stop, she just kept going!)
\c[6](She'd sunk so much time in already, so she might as well continue-)
\c[6](Besides, if she found immortality. That would not just help her dear
friend but everyone else too!)
\c[6](A story about a fox who's constantly trying to please everyone.)
\c[6](He holds a teaparty where he attempts to appeal to everyone's tastes.)
\c[6](He tries to make birds and bugs get along.)
\c[6](The bugs have always loved chocolate, while the birds despise it.)
\c[6](Whereas the birds like seeds while the bugs can't easily bite them.)
\c[6](He made a dish combining seeds and chocolates, wanting everyone to be
happy.)
\c[6](...However, birds are allergic to chocolate and they all fell ill.
Many died.)
\c[6](...And the bugs couldn't easily digest the seeds.)
\c[6](The fox would have done better to just have tried to appeal to one!)
\c[6](Who left this book on the floor... Poor thing!)
\c[6](A tale of a little lemming.)
\c[6](Who believed all those unwilling to jump off cliffs with them were cowards.)
\c[6](And frequently would jump off higher and higher cliffs to prove it.)
\c[6](While he was happy walking alone, many followed him.)
\c[6](Many chased the little lemming.)
\c[6](And many little lemmings were found dead at the bottom of cliffs.)
\c[6](Yet our little lemming marched onwards, despite all.)
\c[6](A story about a Priest performing a sacrifice.)
\c[6](They'd set out to simply sacrifice one offering, for the sake of the community.)
\c[6](But to the Gods' glee, there were two sacrifices that day.)
\c[6](One of the prey, squirming and wriggling.)
\c[6](The other of innocence.)
\c[6](For the Priest handed a ram the knife.)
\c[6](And their little sacrificial sheep found their wool stained red.)
\c[6](Who left this book on the floor... Poor thing!)
\c[6](A story of a court jester.)
\c[6](Frequently this Jester would go to great lengths to entertain the court.)
\c[6](They were favoured by the court.)
\c[6](So much so, the king granted the Jester servants, pages and assistants.)
\c[6](This power got to the Jester's head and they started to believe they were king.)
\c[6](King's don't have consequences, so the Jester acted accordingly.)
\c[6](Testing various spells and hexes on their servants...)
\c[6](It's a wonder they didn't rebel against the little Jester.)
\c[6](A story about a loyal dog.)
\c[6](Who fell in love with a doe, believing them to be their master.)
\c[6](They would do anything for this doe. But the doe held little power.)
\c[6](For you see, they had no antlers.)
\c[6](The Loyal Dog wished to bring their master power.)
\c[6](So they hunted, deer by deer, knocking them out and taking pieces of their antlers.)
\c[6](The Dog stitched the antlers together and put them on the Doe's head.)
\c[6](When the doe awoke they were overjoyed, believing it was a miracle.)
\c[6](They achieved everything they had sought.)
\c[6](But when the loyal dog informed the Doe it was their doing...)
\c[6](The Doe was horrified and ran away, vowing to never see the Dog again.)
\c[6](Now the loyal dog patrols the woods, stalking and following their darling Doe.)
\c[6](Ensuring nothing ever harms them.)
\c[6](A tale of a bridge goat who housed a flock of sheep across their sacred bridge.)
\c[6](This Bridge goat was tasked with protecting these sheep with their life.)
\c[6](But the Goat wished they were more than just a simple village bridge goat.)
\c[6](They started parading their horns, making a spectacle of themselves.)
\c[6](Some marvelled, some were annoyed by how the goat showed off.)
\c[6](A wolf taunted the goat, saying their horns were fragile and unimpressive.)
\c[6](The goat insisted their horns could damage even the hardest of enemies.
And invited the wolf to try beating them in a ramming match.)
\c[6](The goat, eager to prove themselves, brought the wolf to their bridge for the match.)
\c[6](The wolf, however, promptly ran past the goat and started devouring the sheep.)
\c[6](And the Goat could not defend them. Merely standing there shocked.)
\c[6](By the end of the day, they were freed of the burden of their bridge.)
\c[6](As there was nothing left in the field to defend.)
\c[6](A story of a grieving set of parents...)
\c[6](They'd lost their darling son far too young and were scared he would be
lonely in the afterlife.)
\c[6](They went to Death and begged and pleaded for their son to have company.)
\c[6](Death obliged and reaped a soul to be his bride.)
\c[6](The two of them had a gorgeous wedding. United in Death.)
\c[6](The parents were overjoyed and showered Death in gold.)
\c[6](Who left this book on the floor... Poor thing!)
\c[6](A book explaining that due to political outcry from anti-ultimate groups
in recent years Hopes Peak has attempted to scout more 'rags to riches' stories
in order to combat claims of them being biased and just making the 'rich get richer.')
\c[6](A book explaining the conception of the Anti-Ultimate movement-)
\c[6](It explains the discontent growing within the general public as more and more
tax money was spent on funding Hopes Peak and Ultimates in general.)
\c[6](An issue that was compounded by already rich and influential people consistently
getting scouted over those who could use the benefits that Hopes Peak provided.)
\c[6](A book about the founding of this Prison..?)
\c[6](A lot of the information here is redacted but it appears to explain how this
prison was founded initially by the government.)
\c[6](...Apparently it was used as an 'ethical' human testing facility. As the public
ruled that prisoners convicted with certain charges could ethically be tested on as
punishment.)
\c[6](...It seems abandoned now though, I wonder what happened.)
\c[6](A book about the 'alice project'... Seems a little too technical
for me to understand, haha-)
\c[6](A scandalous book which tears into Hopes Peak and its history of cover-ups and
sweeping controversies with their Ultimates under the rug whenever it benefited them.)
\c[6](The Book seems a little biased to me...)
\c[6](Wait- these are all 'Midnight' books! These are mine!)
\c[6](Oh... Wait, someone has gone through them and annotated them-)
\c[6](Yikes... Why are they so harsh about them???)
\c[6](A book detailing the founding of 'Rising Hopes Academy'.)
\c[6](One of the many sister schools to Hopes Peak...)
\c[6]('Rising Hopes Academy' focused on immersing students solely in their studies.
So once enrolled you couldn't leave the town the school was in until graduation,
nor access websites or contact people outside of the town.)
\c[6](However, scouts visit there frequently, so it was an easy fast track to get
scouted.)
\c[6](I remember kids from that school were... Weird. There was similarly a general
feeling amongst those of us who were properly scouted that the Rising Hopes kids got
it easy and didn't fully deserve their titles.)
\c[6](A book detailing various successful Ultimates who've graduated from Hopes' Peak.)
\c[6](Although someone has gone through and crossed out all the misinformation and just
generally been mean in their notations...)
\c[6](Who left this book on the floor... Poor thing!)
\c[6](Who left this book on the floor... Poor thing!)
\c[6](A story about a crow who would fly to a sick man's window every morning.)
\c[6](This sick man desired to reunite with his wife, he was too sick for her
to see him.)
\c[6](And so the crow would provide him with a cure each day. A berry.)
\c[6](But no matter how many times the man took the cure, he remained sick.)
\c[6](Little did the man know, his wife was a Witch.)
\c[6](Sending this crow to him to keep poisoning him with the berries.)
\c[6](And the crow obeyed, determined to keep the lovers apart.)
\c[6](Who left this book on the floor... Poor thing!)
\c[6](A book that seems to be about the Olympian Gods... But it's written in a strange
order...)
\c[6]('01- Apollo: A brother God, his poetry had profound influence on mortals. Often to
dangerous extents. All his lovers, both male and female, face terrible fates.')
\c[6]('02- Hermes: A diety of both Chthonic and Olympian status, one winged sandle in
each world. He happily played both sides and was quick to trick his fellow Gods for
his own benefit.')
\c[6]('03- Ares: Endless, impulsive violence without thought. Unconcerned with his own
thoughts, unconcerned with consequences. Simply looking for a rush.')
\c[6]('04- Artemis: Huntress Goddess, when she starts a hunt her prey's fate is already
decided. A twin diety and punisher of men.')
\c[6]('05- Poseidon: The original king of the Gods, replaced by time. Strong leader,
willing to punish those who harm his family without mercy.')
\c[6]('06- Hephaestus: Isolated God, focused solely on creation. Despite his solitude, he
holds on to his connections as if they are his property. Focusing on how he can retain
them physically with little concern for their emotions.')
\c[6]('07- Dionysus: Endless self indulgence and spectacle, often with great harmful
consequences for others. This harm fails to mean anything if it allows the God to
reaffirm his position.')
\c[6]('08- Athena: A Goddess of the mind, focused on planning and forethought. However,
when provoked she will stand on the front line and combat with ruthless violence.')
\c[6]('09- Zeus: King of the Gods, can avoid justice on account of being emblematic
of justice in itself. Acts upon this indiscriminately and indulgently.')
\c[6]('10- Hera: Keeper of Oaths and promises. Protector of the family and the
sanctity of unions and households. Will punish those who violates or harms these
units accordingly and will do anything to uphold these unions.')
\c[6]('11- Demeter: Goddess of the Harvest. Cares deeply for the earth, but even
more so for her family. Will bring great destructive harm to anyone who dares to
tear her family apart.')
\c[6]('12- Aphrodite: Bringer of overwhelming, overpowering love. Love so all consuming
it becomes dangerous and corruptive, driving one to the point of mania...')
